title: The Great Sorting Adventure
markdown:
The sun burst over the horizon, splashing the sky with brilliant pinks and fiery oranges! Kian the boat fixer popped his eyes open. His workshop! Usually so tidy, with tools polished and hung just-so. But today… oh, pickle pots! The big sorting bin, stuffed with bits from every boat repair, was overflowing! It spilled its jumbled contents onto the wooden floor like a giant, messy splash. "Oh, pickle pots and putty knives!" Kian cried, his eyes wide with surprise.

Dottie the duck waddled in, her feathers a little ruffled. "Quack! What a mess, Kian! It looks like a treasure chest blew up!" she giggled, her head bobbing.

Kian spotted Uncle Hari, polishing the speedy blue hull of "The Zip." Uncle Hari knew all about making boats zoom. "Uncle Hari!" Kian called, pointing. "We need a tiny, shiny screw for The Zip's special propeller! It’s vital for its speed! It’s somewhere in this… this jumble!"

Uncle Hari smiled, a twinkle in his eye. "A challenge? A grand adventure awaits! Let's get to it!"

They peered into the bin. It was a puzzle of forgotten things: crinkly papers, clanky metal bits, smooth glass jars, and bendy plastic toys. Kian dug with his hands. "Too many things! All mixed up!"

Dottie nudged a paper. "Quack! This paper is soft! That metal bit is hard!"

Uncle Hari chuckled. "See the differences? That's your clue! Sort them by what they are made of!"

Kian tilted his head. "Different? Like this paper rips easily, but this metal spoon is tough?"

Dottie dipped her head. "And this glass bottle doesn't bend! But this squishy plastic cup bends!"

"Exactly!" Uncle Hari beamed. "Put all the papers here, the metal bits there, the glass yonder, and the plastic in its own pile!"

Kian’s eyes lit up. "That's it! Piles!"

With a quick waddle, they set to work. Kian stacked blueprints. "Paper pile!" he announced. Dottie nudged a bent fork. "Metal pile, quack!" she chirped. Uncle Hari placed a glass jar. "Glass pile," he said softly. They found a plastic boat toy. "Plastic pile!" Kian declared.

Soon, four neat piles stretched across the floor: paper, metal, glass, plastic. Kian peered into the metal pile. Amidst nuts and bolts, something glinted. "Aha!" he shouted, his voice filled with glee. "The shiny screw!"

Dottie quacked excitedly. "You found it! The metal pile worked! Hooray for sorting!"

Uncle Hari patted Kian’s shoulder. "When you sort things by what they are made of, it's easier to find what you need. We can use these bits again! That’s recycling. It helps keep our harbour tidy and our world cleaner!"

Kian grinned, holding up the screw. "Sorting is super smart!" He looked at the piles. "I wonder what else we can find if we sort things properly!" The messy bin had turned into a brilliant lesson. Kian, Dottie, and Uncle Hari felt ready for whatever exciting adventures the bright, busy day might bring.
characters: Kian the boat fixer, Dottie the duck, Uncle Hari
